architecture.pattern: offline-first with a static edge and a cloud used only for identity and data
architecture.summary: The client runs entirely on the device (native or browser) with a local database. The cloud serves static files, handles identity and, in a later stage, sync. There is no application server of its own: a backend is added only when measured demand justifies it.

components.technology: Outbox pattern, written in the same transaction as the change
components.role: Local queue of changes, ready to be sent to the cloud

components.role: Target of upload sync and, later, of device-to-device download sync

limits.note: 2 OCPUs running continuously after the 2026 cut; the test checks whether paid accounts keep 4. The documentation disagrees: the Always Free resources page says 1,500 for all accounts, while the ARM compute page and the price list still show 3,000 OCPU-hours and 18,000 GB-hours. The effective limit stays unproven until the month closes. Read on 2026-11-22: 2,027 OCPU-hours used in November, 527 of them above 1,500, all at zero cost; the projection for the month is 2,879, below 3,000. That is strong evidence, not proof, that the limit is 3,000

services.note: Oracle may reclaim an idle instance (95th percentile of CPU, network and memory below 20% over 7 days). The stop planned for 2026-11-18 was waived by the owner: the monthly 1,500 OCPU-hours was crossed on 2026-11-16 and cost stayed at zero, so the VM keeps running as the default executor for builds, tests and publishing, and is stopped only if a Compute charge appears. On 2026-11-01, seven days after creation, the VM was still running, had not been reclaimed, and the month's cost was zero; this does not prove the account is exempt from reclamation. Since 2026-11-22 the VM also hosts the CI runner (dedicated user without sudo, systemd service, outbound connections only); it uses only boot-disk space and does not change the shape or the hours

services.role: VM boot disk (50 of 200 GB in use)

protections.description: A tenancy quota zeroes compute and block storage and allows only the free A1, including the regional count. During the test, the applied quota allows 4 OCPUs and 24 GB on the A1 and, at that value, does not block the 1,500 OCPU-hour overage; the budget is what warns about cost
protections.verification: resource-availability shows only the A1 available; other shapes at 0

protections.description: Monthly budget of 1 unit of the tenancy currency with an alert from 0.01 of actual spend
A scheduled monitor reads the VM's hours and cost every 6 hours and alerts at 80%, 95% and 100% of the 3,000 OCPU-hour and 18,000 GB-hour ceiling; the VM is stopped only if a Compute charge appears

services.role: Server-side operations of the app (production and beta)
services.note: On 2026-11-22 the production functions were republished from the main branch: 9 are active in production at no cost, including one triggered by a Firestore document creation through Eventarc (free for Google-source events). Functions in this region spend the quota faster, upload the source to a bucket outside the quota and pay for internet egress, because the Cloud Run egress quota applies only to North America. Each deploy leaves about 0.55 to 0.6 GiB of images in Artifact Registry, which a 1-day cleanup policy removes; the free tier is 0.5 GiB-month accumulated per account, so several deploys a day can exceed it. In production, 4 of the 6 free secret versions are in use
Deleted together with the image repository: zero requests in 365 days and no reference in the code

practices: TDD: the test fails for the right reason before the implementation
Compiler warnings treated as errors; XML documentation required in CI
Security headers and CSP tested end to end
Service worker tested end to end: returns to the app from the cache and opens offline
Service worker hardened against a redirected response from the edge, with a simulated redirect in the end-to-end tests
Every release checked by script the way a client would see it: headers, wasm type, environment, second visit, service worker cache and offline open
SonarQube Cloud quality gate on pull requests
Git pre-commit hook that scans the staged content and blocks a secret before the commit exists
Third-party actions pinned to the full commit SHA, not to a tag
Upgrade tested on the published beta: the app opens with the profile written by the previous version and checks that local data survives; the profile is kept only if the run is green
The .NET SDK and workload set pinned in a version file, so beta and production publish with the same runtime
Production published only by manual dispatch, with a typed confirmation and only commits that already passed a green beta
The self-hosted runner serves only push and manual-dispatch runs of the staging and main branches, never pull requests, so code from a PR cannot read the deploy secrets

Production moved to the self-hosted runner only after a rollback to the previous Worker version was rehearsed in both directions, and a repository variable returns the jobs to hosted runners in seconds
Dependency updates in monthly PRs, with a 14-day wait and no major versions of the .NET packages
Local Firebase (emulators) as the default target; the real project only when the emulator does not respond
A test is labeled flaky only after its class filter has been run 5 to 8 times; two unstable synchronization tests were stabilized this way

Static-analysis findings are fixed in the code (cognitive complexity, unawaited promises); a false positive, such as a public client key or a deliberately invalid test password, is marked with a written justification
Per-file documentation in a mirror of the tree, with invariants and reasons rather than signatures

process: Every delivery goes through specification, plan, TDD execution, independent review and fixes with tests
Minor review findings are recorded with an owner and a time to resolve them
Development assisted by specialized agents per layer (domain, data, UI, hosts, e2e, review, debugging, documentation research, cloud)
Each agent has a model and effort level set by the type of work, and an orchestration step decides what runs in parallel and how to evaluate what comes back
This showcase is updated from a sanitized fact package: the README data blocks and the ADRs are generated by script, and CI (facts, leaks, secrets and SonarQube Cloud) blocks any PR that fails
Each cloud has a versioned file of free-tier quotas, checked against the official source, with an operational limit of 80%
Cloud operations (publishing, checking resources, costs and quotas) go through an infrastructure agent called by the main session, with mandatory checks and the pitfalls already hit on record
